lessons.title: Seeing in Numbers
lessons.content_md:
# Computer Vision 👁️

Humans look at a photo and instantly see a cat, a tree, or a stop sign. But a computer doesn't have eyes. To a computer, an image is just a massive grid of numbers.

## The Pixel Grid

If you zoom into a digital photograph far enough, you'll see tiny squares called **Pixels**. Each pixel is represented by numbers that describe its color.

For a black and white image, the number might be 0 for pure black and 255 for pure white. 

When you feed an image into an AI, you aren't feeding it a picture. You are feeding it an Excel spreadsheet of thousands of numbers.

<flipcard front="🔢 How does a computer see an image?" back="As a giant 2D array (a grid) of numbers, where every number represents the color intensity of a single pixel."></flipcard>

## Finding Edges

So how does the AI turn those numbers into a "cat"? It uses a special kind of hidden layer called a Convolutional Layer.

These layers slide a small "magnifying glass" (called a filter) over the numbers, looking for dramatic changes. If the numbers suddenly jump from 0 (black) to 255 (white), the AI knows it just found a hard **Edge**.

By finding all the edges, it can find shapes. By finding shapes, it can find objects.

<flipcard front="📐 How does AI find an object in an image?" back="It scans the grid of numbers for sudden mathematical changes, which represent the edges and outlines of shapes."></flipcard>

<flipcard front="🚗 Why is Computer Vision important?" back="It's how self-driving cars 'see' pedestrians and stop signs, and how medical AI detects tumors in X-rays!"></flipcard>
